mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the shareholder's country of formation (e.g., Companies Registry of Hong Kong SAR; Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority of Singapore; State Administration for Market Regulation of the PRC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent Apostille authority of the country of origin (e.g., High Court of Hong Kong SAR; Singapore Academy of Law; PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passports and residential-address evidence of every natural-person ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 25% or more of the target SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity authority of each UBO's country of residence (e.g., HKSAR Immigration Department; Immigration & Checkpoints Authority of Singapore; Public Security Bureau of the PRC)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent national authority; for non-Apostille Convention states, Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and/or Register of Directors and Shareholders of each holding-company shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered corporate services provider / incorporated secretary or equivalent fiduciary of the foreign holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, accompanied by sworn translation into French, German, or English certified before a Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for the capital deposit (minimum statutory SARL capital EUR 12,000)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or licensed trust company of the parent investor structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank-sealed attestation notarized in the country of origin, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney and board/shareholders' resolution authorizing the Luxembourg incorporation signatories and the initial manager or managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General meeting or board of directors of the foreign sole shareholder or controlling shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the jurisdiction of execution

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated; particularly Title V (Articles 100–161) on the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating through the eJustice portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and notarized coordinated articles of association (statuts)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital is EUR 12,000 for a SARL. The capital must be fully subscribed and each share paid up in cash or in kind before incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into an escrow/blocked bank account held in the company's name, released only on completion of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The undersigned shareholders of [Company Name] S.à r.l. hereby adopt the following unanimous written resolutions: (1) The share capital of EUR 12,000 is fully subscribed by the shareholders as detailed in the subscription schedule. (2) Each share is accepted, and capital contributions are credited to a blocked bank account in the company's name, to be released upon registration. (3) The registered office is established at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. (4) [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant), with full authority to represent the company. (5) The manager is instructed to complete all filing, publication, and tax registration formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg bank or credit institution approved by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the future SARL and deposit the entire share capital (EUR 12,000 or higher). Request an escrow certificate (attestation de blocage) from the bank, confirming that the funds are blocked until the notary submits the deed of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proof of residential address of managers and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML/KYC documentation, provide comprehensive source-of-wealth evidence and a renewed instruction letter; the application may also be resubmitted through another approved credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarize articles of incorporation and by-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to verify legal capacity, review the articles, and execute the formal notarial deed of incorporation. The notary coordinates the release of the blocked capital for the incorporation and files the deed with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of shareholders and managers
Details of the registered office and consent of the property owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a legal or formal objection, amend the articles to satisfy Luxembourg law and reschedule signature before the same or another notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company in the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, file the deed and annexes online via the eJustice portal or directly with LBR. Pay the registration fee. LBR examines the file and issues an RCS extract (extrait) confirming legal personality and registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of address or lease for the registered office
Criminal record certificates or equivalent for managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If LBR issues a query or incompleteness notice, respond with corrected or additional documents within the prescribed deadline; after rectification, resubmission will be processed as a regular application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Electronic Collection of Companies and Associations (RESA) / eJustice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or the company submits a publication notice to RESA within one month of RCS registration, including the RCS registration number and an abstract of the statutes, as required by Luxembourg law.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice is rejected, correct the abstract and resubmit; late publication may be regularized with a supplementary filing and may carry limited retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with tax and social administrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the corporate registration forms, obtain the RC (corporate tax) number, VAT reference and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) file. Register with CCSS if the company has employees, or declare an absence of employees.
required_dossiers: Bank account details of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where forms are incomplete, the ACD or AEDT will issue a deficiency notice; respond online with the missing documentation before any default assessment or penalty is imposed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) — prudential supervision of specialized real estate investment undertakings
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CSSF authorisation and approval as a specialized real estate investment undertaking (société d'investissement immobilier / SII) under the Luxembourg Law of 11 February 2010 on real estate investment undertakings, as amended

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et de la Biodiversité — Administration de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-dependent: Exempt for passive rental properties; Registration or simplified environmental evaluation for small- and medium-scale building works; Full EIA report for major construction projects listed under Annexes I and II of the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment law.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 21 December 2012; VOC and air emissions thresholds under EU Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) where applicable; waste storage and disposal in accordance with Luxembourg waste-management legislation; energy performance and technical building standards under the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive and related Grand-Ducal regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), structural load inspection by a certified engineer, and occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) for any office, maintenance or operational staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) (direct corporate income tax, net wealth tax) and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) (VAT, registration duties), both under the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; primary official portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu; corporate legal entity registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SARL, the statutory sequence is: (i) execute a notarized deed of incorporation in Luxembourg; (ii) file with the RCS/Luxembourg Business Registers to obtain the legal entity 'matricule' registration number; (iii) obtain the 11-digit Luxembourg identification number (numéro d'immatriculation) from the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD); (iv) register for VAT with AEDT using the standard VAT registration form (Form n°1 or electronic channel via MyGuichet), receiving a Luxembourg VAT identification number formatted as LU + 8 digits; (v) complete employer and withholding tax registrations if hiring staff; (vi) activate the electronic filing credential (TVA eCDF / MyGuichet authentication). Non-resident corporate investors may directly register through an accredited tax representative when required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply US-style check-the-box classification. Under Luxembourg law, a SARL is per se subject to entity-level corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), and net wealth tax, with imputation of withholding tax on dividends. Available elective mechanisms include: (i) Luxembourg fiscal unity / tax consolidation for CIT purposes (intégration fiscale) by a resident parent holding at least 95% of a resident subsidiary; (ii) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) per Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; (iii) election of the 80% IP exemption box regime (R&D qualifying assets); (iv) ATAD-compliant hybrid mismatch restriction disclosures; (v) participation exemption election for dividends and capital gains under strict holding thresholds and substance requirements. No full tax-transparency election is available for an SARL under Luxembourg domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi du 12 février 1979, as amended) and Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for the domestic small-business franchise (régime de la franchise) below which small established Luxembourg businesses may be exempt, subject to option to be taxed; non-established foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg do not generally benefit from a quantitative threshold and must register for Luxembourg VAT from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg, unless a special simplification regime (typically one-stop-shop or reverse-charge) applies. Threshold figures and franchise provisions are subject to annual EU small-business harmonization updates.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: As of the filing date, Luxembourg does not operate a mandatory real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC) clearance mechanism for business-to-business invoices. E-invoicing is permitted under EU VAT invoice rules, and electronic invoices are accepted if authenticity/legibility requirements are met. For public procurement (B2G) invoices, Luxembourg mandates e-invoicing through the national Peppol-compliant platform. No API stamping or real-time clearance with AEDT is required for domestic B2B invoices yet; taxpayers must nonetheless retain full invoice data for audits. Luxembourg is aligning with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposal, under which future electronic invoice reporting obligations will be introduced.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Luxembourg VAT is available when the title/vendor supplies goods that are physically transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union (export zero rate), or when goods are dispatched to another EU Member State in an intra-Community supply where purchasing VAT ID is valid and the EC Sales List / recapitulative statement is filed. Services are zero-rated or exempt when the place of supply is treated as outside Luxembourg (e.g., B2B services supplied to a non-EU customer where reverse-charge transfers liability, or services directly linked to exported goods under Article 162 of the VAT Code). Conditions include proof of physical dispatch within statutory time limits, retention of transport and commercial documents, and good-faith compliance with the standard VAT invoice requirements; the exporter must be the VAT-registered taxable person and act in a business context.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/Exit Summary Declaration), customs endorsed exit evidence from the EU border
Bill of Lading or air waybill (AWB) evidencing international transport from Luxembourg
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank payment/swift confirmation evidencing the economic transfer of proceeds
Commercial invoice, packing list, the zero-rated supply invoice, and transport contract (CMR or CIM)
Proof of export regularity (export holder authorizations, lodged T1 / T2 documents when relevant)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities conduct targeted scrutiny of export zero-rating claims, cross-referencing customs data, transport and payment documentation. Where zero-rating is denied, the full VAT is reassessed with late-payment interest from the due date; penalties range from administrative fines (usually EUR 250 to EUR 10,000 per breach) to tax fraud penalties of up to EUR 250,000, plus possible imprisonment for up to 5 years, with retrospective clawback of input VAT recovery and extraterritorial or group liability under joint and several liability rules. Deductions taken against a fraudulent export claim may be disallowed, and the limitation period for tax fraud investigations may be extended to 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); exchange and capital-movement supervision is shared with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), while monetary policy and TARGET2 settlement are administered by the European Central Bank within the Eurosystem. The Luxembourg Ministry of Finance retains residual competence for exceptional safeguard measures under TFEU Articles 64-66.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full current- and capital-account convertibility without foreign-exchange controls, licensing, surrender, or prior-approval barriers on investment, financing, distribution, or liquidation flows. The euro is freely convertible for all treasury operations of this real estate investment trust. Profit remittance is unrestricted at the FX/treasury level, but dividends paid by the SARL attract Luxembourg withholding tax at 15% (potentially 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders, or reduced under applicable double tax treaties). Capital gains, principal repayments, and liquidation proceeds are not subject to withholding tax and are freely transferable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, repatriation deadline, or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Luxembourg. The REIT may retain, convert, or reinvest foreign-currency income without authorization. Cross-border payments are reported statistically by the executing Luxembourg credit institution to the BCL under the Eurosystem balance-of-payments (BPM6) framework via purpose codes embedded in SWIFT/SEPA messages; direct BCL declarations may be triggered for external financial positions such as intercompany debt or foreign property acquisitions above the applicable BCL threshold. No reporting duty restricts liquidity mobilization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / EUR-USD-GBP multi-currency Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for lettings income and SEPA disbursements
Operational and distribution clearing account / Commercial LC facility
Operational Account with cross-border USD clearing and SWIFT MT103 rails
SEPA-centric Operational Account for recurring property expenses
Treasury/hard-currency account for ISDA derivatives collateral and FX forwards

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium, usable only as an operational cash-flow overlay and never as the primary treasury or escrow bank. A Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institution (EMI) under PSD2 and the Law of 10 November 2009 may hold e-money and execute payment transactions but cannot grant credit, issue guarantees or letters of credit, or provide the escrow, custody, and depositary services required for regulated REIT or RAIF/SIF structures. Third-country EMIs are commonly declined for Luxembourg real estate SPVs because they lack BCL balance-of-payments reporting connectivity and cannot satisfy CSSF-expected custodial controls. EMIs remain acceptable for small operational rails such as property-management fees, utility payments, and contractor rebates, provided the main acquisition, escrow, and dividend flows clear through a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No explicit statutory rule mandates physical attendance for corporate account opening; however, CSSF AML expectations require identification of directors and beneficial owners to a reliable standard. In market practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one legal representative (director or authorized agent with certified power of attorney) to attend a client onboarding interview in Luxembourg for a first-time institutional relationship, especially when the Capital Escrow Account will receive third-country funding. Remote opening is possible where: (i) beneficial owners are resident in FATF member jurisdictions; (ii) video identification is performed using eIDAS-qualified trust services accepted by the bank; (iii) corporate documents are apostilled and, where necessary, legalized; and (iv) the bank obtains a professional reference from recognized Luxembourg counsel or a notary. A Luxembourg notary or a CSSF-regulated PFS may accelerate the interview and document-collection process on the bank's behalf.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection originates from an investor in a FATF grey-listed or EU non-cooperative jurisdiction, or passes through an intermediary without a recognized banking license.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized organizational chart of the shareholder cascade; RBE extract; tax residency certificates; audited financial statements; bank reference letter from the first remitting institution; sworn source-of-funds declaration; sanctions and adverse-media screening evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque share-capital funding or shareholder loans from a non-EEA related party lacking documented economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital contribution deed and loan agreement; board minutes approving the financing; drawdown notices; transfer pricing policy and arm's-length interest-rate benchmark; MT103 remittance evidence with purpose codes; confirmation of debt purpose and traceability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Real estate acquisition involving potentially sanctioned counterparties, unverified property values, or tenant funds that cannot be sourced.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent valuation report from a RICS/CREPS-accredited valuer; notarial purchase deed; lease schedule with tenant KYC files; energy certificates and insurance policies; escrow bank confirmation; certified statement that all parties have been screened against EU, OFAC, and UN consolidated sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors, UBOs, or authorized signatories are politically exposed persons (PEPs), or ownership is held through arrangements that conceal natural persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-assessment and declaration forms; legal opinion addressing the ownership chain and legitimacy of wealth; source-of-wealth documentation (sale deeds, inheritance instruments, employment contracts, corporate distributions); confirmation that the SARL has no bearer shares (statutorily prohibited); written enhanced-monitoring undertaking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting challenge that the entity operates an unlicensed fund or REIT activity requiring CSSF authorization or a depositary, creating regulatory uncertainty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CSSF license or RAIF/SIF registration certificate, or a legal opinion confirming the SARL's status as an unregulated special-purpose real-estate holding company outside the fund authorization perimeter; AIFM appointment agreement if applicable; depositary letter executed with a Luxembourg credit institution; audited business plan; undertaking to notify the bank of any CSSF authorization trigger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital (share capital, share premium, and shareholder loans) must be routed exclusively into the dedicated Capital Escrow Account at the chosen Luxembourg Tier-1 bank. Remittances are executed by the investor via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV for cover aggregations), with the beneficiary field displaying the exact legal name, the LU IBAN, and the escrow sub-account reference. The remitter's bank must be instructed to include the BCL/Eurosystem balance-of-payments purpose code for 'Direct Investment – Equity' or 'Direct Investment – Intercompany Lending' in the structured reference field; where the remitter's clearing system requires an ISO 20022 purpose code, the equivalent code is entered at the executing bank's discretion. Before escrow release to the operational account, the bank's compliance function verifies: (i) the board resolution approving the capital call; (ii) the notarized subscription deed or loan agreement; (iii) the RBE extract evidencing beneficial owners; (iv) source-of-funds documentation for amounts above EUR 1,000,000; and (v) sanctions and adverse-media screening. Settlement is executed via TARGET2 for EUR or via the bank's USD/EUR correspondent network; SEPA Credit Transfer may be used for euro contributions from EEA shareholders where eligible, but MT103 is preferred for auditability. Intra-group funding must be contracted on arm's-length terms and supported by transfer pricing documentation to satisfy both the bank and Luxembourg tax authorities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR-denominated disbursements to EEA contractors, property managers, insurers, and tax authorities are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT/SCT Inst) and SEPA Direct Debit (SDD Core/B2B). Large acquisitions and refurbishment contracts settled outside the EEA are executed through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers; where documentary security is required, the bank issues or advises commercial letters of credit under MT700/MT707 (UCP600) for imports of materials and construction equipment, with transport documents collected through the presenting bank. Dividend and profit distributions are remitted via SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA beneficiaries, or via SWIFT MT103 with MT202 COV for non-EEA investors; for institutional US recipients, the bank's US correspondent clears distributions through ACH/Fedwire rails. The distribution sub-account is funded at least one TARGET2 business day before payment date. Every outgoing cross-border instruction carries the appropriate BCL balance-of-payments purpose code and is screened against sanctions, PEP, and fraud lists prior to release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright single-currency FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) with tenors up to 24 months, hedging rental income, purchase prices, and distribution cash flows; executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA margin and EMIR clearing requirements.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps converting foreign-currency acquisition debt (USD/GBP) into EUR floating-rate exposure, subject to EMIR clearing and margin rules.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies without deliverable offshore markets, where an underlying real-estate rental or sale exposure exists and physical settlement is legally impaired.

Vanilla FX options (EUR call/put) purchased to protect minimum repatriation yields on foreign-currency distribution streams; writing uncovered options is not permissible without CSSF consent and an economic-hedge memorandum.
Short-dated FX swaps for liquidity management between Treasury sub-accounts at the same bank, used exclusively to settle cross-currency positions without speculative open positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) filed with the Luxembourg commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the general meeting; general meeting must occur within six months of financial year-end, so no later than seven months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties ranging from EUR 40 to EUR 4,000 per document; criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and risk of administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution for persistent non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO declaration) in the Luxembourg RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month of the registration anniversary; additionally within one month of any change in beneficial ownership, including share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 for non-declaration or false declaration; longer non-compliance may lead to administrative penalties, publication of default status, and restrictions on distributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year entities, generally 31 May after the tax year; extensions may be granted by AEDT upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return penalty of 10% of assessed tax; late payment interest at 0.8% per month on amounts due; tax authorities may issue an ex officio assessment if return is omitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the corporate income tax return; due 31 May following the relevant tax year for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return penalty of 10% of the amount due; statutory late interest of 0.8% per month; assessment by AEDT in case of failure to file

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if a SARL exceeds two of three criteria: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce of 50 employees. A Luxembourg REIT vehicle is generally required to appoint an independent auditor irrespective of thresholds due to applicable investment fund regulation and public-interest status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial and companies register and annual accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted or required for listed entities and certain regulated investment vehicles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every Luxembourg SARL must register with the RBE before RCS registration and must confirm the accuracy of its beneficial-ownership data annually within one month of the registration anniversary. Any transfer of shares must be reported within one month; the annual confirmation represents an updated statutory declaration and failure to confirm can result in criminal fines and distribution restrictions.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate headline rate (Luxembourg City, tax year 2024-2025): 17% corporate income tax (IRC) on taxable income above EUR 175,000 (15% on the first EUR 175,000) + 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC (equal to 1.19%) + municipal business tax (MBT) of 6.75% applied by Luxembourg City. The MBT is deductible for IRC purposes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains where the shareholding is at least 10% or the acquisition cost is at least EUR 1,200,000 and the shares are held for an uninterrupted 12-month period. IP box regime: 80% exemption of net qualifying intellectual property income, producing an effective rate of approximately 5% (OECD nexus compliant). No statutory REIT distribution-ready regime applies to a SARL; rental income from the real estate portfolio is fully subject to ordinary CIT at the aggregate 24.94% rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carry-forward; no time limit and no loss carry-back permitted; carry-forward is forfeited upon loss-trafficking changes of ownership or certain mergers)
